sg.ra: Center Orchestra seats from AAA through D are among the best views in the house. Consider Row A instead of AAA or AA if you do not want to sit extremely close to the stage.
Avoid the side orchestra seats because they are not very comfortable.

This is one of the theater’s best sections, with clear and close elevated views across all four rows. Choose Row A in the Center section for the strongest overall view. Favor center seats over the sides, which are more angled and restricted.
Choose Rows E or F for unobstructed stage views. Avoid side and rear seats when possible because their angle can obscure parts of the stage.
They are private, but the view is more side-on.

sn.c: The Mezzanine overhang starts at row J, so seats behind it may lose a little of the top of the stage.
sn.sh: Overhang may trim the top of the stage

sn.c: Orchestra views are mostly clear, but from the far sides only part of the stage is visible.
sn.sh: Far side seats get a partial view

sn.c: The Boxes beside the Orchestra are private but very angled, giving a side-on view of the stage.
sn.sh: Private, but very angled side-on views

sn.c: In the Front Mezzanine, taller people are likely to feel very cramped in row A. Aisle seats have more legroom.
sn.sh: Row A is very cramped for taller people

sn.c: Side seats are more restricted in every section, most of all in the Rear Mezzanine, where they are farthest away and partly cut off.
sn.sh: Side seats are far away and cut off

sn.lo: Center Rear Mezzanine, rows E to F
sn.c: The front Rear Mezzanine rows E and F are good value, with a clear view down to the stage that nobody in front blocks.
sn.sh: Front rows E and F give a clear view for less

vs.sum: The Lena Horne Theatre offers good sightlines from most seats, with clear views even from the rear mezzanine. The sound quality is well-balanced across the theater. However, the seating is quite tight, especially for taller patrons, which affects comfort. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historic architecture and restored interior, providing a charming atmosphere.

acc.note: Step-free entry and Orchestra. 5 wheelchair seats. No elevators.
